\chapter{Learning Theory — Episode}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.LearningTheory.Hedge.Episode
\section{Overview}

This module develops the adaptive-episode framework for the Hedge algorithm.
It introduces the notions of a loss history, learner policy, and adaptive adversary,
then constructs the canonical generated episode by running the learner/adversary
interaction recursively, and shows that Hedge's tight regret bound carries over
to every such adaptive episode.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Loss history]
\lean{LossHistory}
\leanok
$\texttt{LossHistory}\ N\ t$ is the type of length-$t$ histories of loss vectors
for $N$ experts: it is the function type $\mathrm{Fin}\,t \to \mathrm{Fin}\,N \to \mathbb{R}$,
recording all loss vectors that have been revealed in the past $t$ rounds.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[History to loss sequence]
\lean{LossHistory.toLossSeq}
\leanok
\uses{LossHistory, LossSeq}
Given a history $h : \texttt{LossHistory}\ N\ t$, $\text{\texttt{LossHistory.toLossSeq}}\ h$ coerces it
to a $\texttt{LossSeq}\ N\ t$, enabling the reuse of definitions and theorems from
the pathwise Hedge formalization that are stated over finite loss sequences.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Learner policy]
\lean{LearnerPolicy}
\leanok
\uses{LossHistory}
A $\texttt{LearnerPolicy}\ N$ is a deterministic online strategy for a learner
interacting with $N$ experts: it provides a weight function
$\mathrm{weights} : (t : \mathbb{N}) \to \texttt{LossHistory}\ N\ t \to \mathrm{Fin}\,N \to \mathbb{R}$
together with proofs that the weights are nonnegative and sum to one,
so that the weight vector at each round forms a valid mixed strategy.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Adaptive adversary]
\lean{AdaptiveAdversary}
\leanok
\uses{LossHistory}
An $\texttt{AdaptiveAdversary}\ N$ is an online strategy for the adversary:
it provides a loss-selection function
$\mathrm{loss} : (t : \mathbb{N}) \to \texttt{LossHistory}\ N\ t \to (\mathrm{Fin}\,N \to \mathbb{R}) \to \mathrm{Fin}\,N \to \mathbb{R}$
that maps the current round index, the past loss history, and the learner's
current mixed strategy to a loss vector, subject to the validity condition
that every coordinate of the chosen loss vector lies in $[0, 1]$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Hedge learner policy]
\lean{hedgePolicy}
\leanok
\uses{LearnerPolicy, LossHistory.toLossSeq, hedgeDist, hedgeDist_nonneg, hedgeDist_sum}
$\texttt{hedgePolicy}\ N\ \eta$ is the $\texttt{LearnerPolicy}$ that implements the
Hedge algorithm with learning rate $\eta > 0$: at each round $t$ and for each
loss history $h$, the weights are given by $\texttt{hedgeDist}\ \eta\ (\text{\texttt{LossHistory.toLossSeq}}\ h)\ t$,
the exponential-weights distribution derived from the past realized losses.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Episode loss at natural time]
\lean{episodeLossNat}
\leanok
\uses{AdaptiveAdversary, LearnerPolicy}
$\texttt{episodeLossNat}\ \mathrm{learner}\ \mathrm{adversary}\ t : \mathrm{Fin}\,N \to \mathbb{R}$
is the loss vector produced at round $t$ when the learner and adversary interact
adaptively: the adversary sees the prefix of losses from rounds $0, \ldots, t-1$
and the learner's mixed strategy for round $t$, then returns the loss vector for
round $t$.  The definition is well-founded because the recursion only refers to
strictly earlier rounds.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Episode loss sequence]
\lean{episodeLossSeq}
\leanok
\uses{AdaptiveAdversary, LearnerPolicy, LossSeq, episodeLossNat}
$\texttt{episodeLossSeq}\ T\ \mathrm{learner}\ \mathrm{adversary} : \texttt{LossSeq}\ N\ T$
is the finite loss sequence realized over $T$ rounds by running the learner
against the adaptive adversary, obtained by restricting $\texttt{episodeLossNat}$
to the first $T$ rounds.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Episode]
\lean{Episode}
\leanok
\uses{AdaptiveAdversary, LearnerPolicy, LossSeq, episodeLossSeq}
An $\texttt{Episode}\ N\ T$ packages a learner policy, an adaptive adversary, and
a finite loss sequence of length $T$ for $N$ experts, together with a consistency
proof that the stored loss sequence equals the one generated by running
$\texttt{episodeLossSeq}\ T\ \mathrm{learner}\ \mathrm{adversary}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Generated episode]
\lean{Episode.generated}
\leanok
\uses{AdaptiveAdversary, Episode, LearnerPolicy, episodeLossSeq}
$\texttt{Episode.generated}\ \mathrm{learner}\ \mathrm{adversary}$ is the canonical
$\texttt{Episode}\ N\ T$ constructed by taking the loss sequence to be exactly
$\texttt{episodeLossSeq}\ T\ \mathrm{learner}\ \mathrm{adversary}$; the consistency
condition is satisfied by reflexivity.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Validity of generated episode loss sequence]
\lean{episodeLossSeq_valid}
\leanok
\uses{AdaptiveAdversary, LearnerPolicy, LossSeq.Valid, episodeLossNat, episodeLossSeq}
\difficulty{3}
For any learner policy and adaptive adversary, the generated loss sequence
$\texttt{episodeLossSeq}\ T\ \mathrm{learner}\ \mathrm{adversary}$ is valid,
meaning every entry lies in $[0, 1]$.  Validity is inherited directly from the
adversary's range condition.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Episode losses are valid]
\lean{Episode.losses_valid}
\leanok
\uses{Episode, LossSeq.Valid, episodeLossSeq_valid}
\difficulty{2}
For any $\texttt{Episode}\ N\ T$, the stored loss sequence $\mathrm{episode.losses}$
is valid, i.e., every loss coordinate lies in $[0, 1]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Hedge regret bound for adaptive episodes]
\lean{hedge_regret_bound_tight_episode}
\leanok
\uses{AdaptiveAdversary, episodeLossSeq, episodeLossSeq_valid, hedgePolicy, hedge_regret_bound_tight, regret}
\difficulty{1}
For any $N, T \ge 1$, learning rate $\eta > 0$, and adaptive adversary,
the regret of the Hedge policy with rate $\eta$ on the generated episode
satisfies
\[
  \mathrm{regret}(\eta,\; \texttt{episodeLossSeq}\ T\ (\texttt{hedgePolicy}\ N\ \eta)\ \mathrm{adversary})
  \;\le\; \frac{\ln N}{\eta} + \frac{\eta T}{8}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Hedge regret bound from a packaged episode]
\lean{hedge_regret_bound_tight_of_episode}
\leanok
\uses{Episode, hedgePolicy, hedge_regret_bound_tight_episode, regret}
\difficulty{2}
Let $\mathrm{episode}$ be an $\texttt{Episode}\ N\ T$ whose learner equals
$\texttt{hedgePolicy}\ N\ \eta$ for some $\eta > 0$.  Then
\[
  \mathrm{regret}(\eta,\; \mathrm{episode.losses}) \;\le\; \frac{\ln N}{\eta} + \frac{\eta T}{8}.
\]
\end{theorem}
